name: Cinnabar
toxicityNote: TOXIC: cinnabar is mercury sulfide. Do not ingest, make elixirs, grind or heat. Wash hands after handling, keep from children and pets, and seal tumbled or carved pieces. Handle only polished or sealed specimens.
spiritual: Associated with the vital force in Chinese tradition
physical: Kept nearby by people seeking energy
Linked in folklore to warmth and stamina
summary: Cinnabar is a vivid scarlet mercury sulfide long prized as the vermilion pigment and used in tradition for vitality and prosperity, but it is toxic to handle.
intro: Cinnabar is the red of lacquer boxes and temple gates. Raw pieces appear as crusts of brilliant scarlet to brick-red crystals on dolomite or quartz, sometimes shining with an adamantine luster. Powdered cinnabar made vermilion, one of the most beloved pigments of history. It is very soft, about 2 to 2.5, and because it is mercury sulfide, it is poisonous in dust or fumes. Most commercial cinnabar jewelry sold today is cinnabar in quartz or lacquerware, but pure cinnabar carvings still exist. Crystal tradition prizes it as a stone of vitality and money luck, but safe handling matters.
history: Cinnabar has been mined for at least 8,000 years, with some of the oldest known workings at Almaden in Spain and Idrija in Slovenia. The Chinese used cinnabar in lacquer, medicine and alchemy, believing it a source of immortality, and many emperors died from mercury poisoning as a result. Romans coveted it as a pigment, and it was the main source of mercury for centuries. Modern knowledge of its toxicity has ended these uses in safe contexts. Its place as a lucky stone in feng shui, associated with the color red, comes from long traditions.
meaning: In the tradition of Chinese lore and modern crystal practice, cinnabar is a stone of vitality and prosperity. Its fiery red is linked to the root and sacral chakras, and used for drive, passion and good fortune in business. Practitioners say it awakens ambition and supports bold action, and it appears in feng shui as a wealth and protection symbol. Emotionally, it is said to warm a flat or timid mood. Traditionally it is associated with stamina and warmth. Because it contains mercury, modern practitioners treat it as a display stone to be viewed, not worn on the skin or handled casually.
howToUse: Display a sealed cinnabar specimen or cinnabar-in-quartz piece in the wealth corner of a home or office. Use it as a visual focus during intention-setting for business or creative drive, without touching your mouth or eyes afterward. Keep it high on a shelf, out of the reach of children and pets. Avoid wearing raw cinnabar against skin; cinnabar in quartz or lacquer is safer. Wash hands after each handling session.
care: Cinnabar is very soft, sensitive to heat and light, and toxic. Never ingest it, never grind it, never heat it and never make elixirs. Keep it dry and do not soak it. Dust with a soft dry brush while wearing gloves. Cleanse with sound or smoke only. Strong light can darken the surface. Store in a sealed container, wash hands after handling, and keep from children and pets.
identify: Genuine cinnabar is bright scarlet with a heavy weight, a vivid red streak and a soft, easily scratched surface. It is commonly confused with red jasper, realgar, carved red resin and dyed stones. Cinnabar is much denser than jasper and leaves a red streak on porcelain. Many cinnabar carvings are actually lacquer or resin. If a piece is labeled cinnabar but is hard and lightweight, it is likely something else.

faq.a: Yes. Cinnabar is mercury sulfide and is toxic if ingested or if dust or fumes are inhaled. Keep it sealed or displayed, wash hands after handling, keep away from children and pets, and never make elixirs.

faq.q: What is cinnabar used for in crystal practice?
faq.a: In crystal and feng shui tradition cinnabar is a stone of vitality, passion and prosperity. People display sealed pieces in wealth corners or on altars as symbols of drive and good fortune.
No. Avoid water and any wet cleaning. Cinnabar is soft, toxic and best cleansed by sound or smoke. Never wash it down a drain or handle it with bare, damp hands.
